description.narrative: The objective is enhanced capacity to produce statistics in line with user needs and EU requirements.

Programmet syftar till att stärka statistikmyndighetens kapacitet att producera statistik av god kvalitet, samt att bidra till ökad tillgänglighet i linje med användarnas behov, samt att att bidra till anpassning till EU:s standarder.

The project aims to improve SSO’s overall capacity to produce and disseminate quality statistics, to provide an increased availability of statistics in accordance with the needs of current and future users, as well as the requirements of the EU acquis in statistics.

Overall, the project has helped SSO to move away from individual efforts and to separate tools toward more organized systems, clearer responsibilities, and more sustainable ways of working.
Although more work is still needed especially in advanced methods, ICT migration, and expanding register-based statistics the basic foundations for long term modernization in line with European and international standards are now in place.
The European Commission (EU progress report for North Macedonia, November 2025) confirms a moderate to good level of preparedness in statistics.
Key Achievements include among other:
- Improved visibility and dissemination with the launch of a new and more user friendly website (www.stat.mk) and strengthened branding.
- ICT modernisation progressed with a defined ICT toolbox, a strategic decision to migrate from SAS to R with a key aspect transforming it into an open-source environment that empowers non-IT staff to manage their own statistical workflows, strengthened data governance (GDPR roadmap and DPO appointment), increased Application Programming Interface (API) usage, which is a technical solution that allows data to be transferred back and forth between software in a formalised way, and initiation of secure remote access solutions.
- A new training centre was completed and is actively used for internal and external capacity building.
-Advanced management systems through the development of the MAKPLAN planning, monitoring, and timereporting system which is supporting more efficient resource use from 2026.
- Internal communication is improved through draft communication guidelines and the start of intranet development.
- Methodological capacity was strengthened through the establishment of an organisationwide methodology support group and initial training.
- Registerbased statistics expanded significantly: use of the Employment Register increased from two to six products, and the Structure of Earnings Survey is now fully registerbased, reducing costs and respondent burden.
- Progress was made toward developing education and population registers, laying the groundwork for future registerbased production.
However, the key challenges remain including:
- Conitnued staff capacity constraints and slowed project implementation in some areas due to competing work priorities.
- Progress in registerbased statistics depends on pending organisational decisions and clarified mandates.
- Also, the SAS-to-R migration and advanced methodological development require continued skills development and change management.
- Administrative data access, particularly in education statistics, remains dependent on final agreements, expected in 2026.
The programme applies Result Based Management using an adaptive management approach. Ongoing monitoring helps identify information gaps, guide decisions, and adjust priorities as needed. Progress, risks, and opportunities are regularly reviewed through Project Management Group meetings and bilateral discussions with SSO and project experts, allowing continuous learning and timely adjustments during implementation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
